title: Hen of the Hissing Vents
story: Pyrrholine squats on the steam vents of Mount Grell, and every time she ruffles her cinder feathers the mountain grumbles louder. Down in the vent-fields live the glass salamanders, far too slow to outrun a lava tide. Mr 6 hitches a ridgeback goat to a stone cart and starts loading.
question: There are 174 glass salamanders, the cart carries 16 of them per load, each load takes 7 minutes to haul to safety, and the mountain will boil over in 80 minutes — how many minutes to spare will Mr 6 have when the last salamander is clear?
solution: Loads needed: 174 / 16 = 10.875, and a part-load still needs a whole trip, so that is 11 loads.
praise: Dividing to find the number of loads was perfect thinking — the step left over was rounding 10.875 UP to 11, because those last 14 salamanders still need a whole cart ride.
hint: First find how many cart loads it takes — and remember a leftover handful of salamanders still needs a full trip of its own.
victory: The last glass salamander clinked into the cart with three whole minutes left, and Pyrrholine laid an enormous ash egg in surprise when she saw the fields already empty.
imagePrompt: An enormous soot-feathered hen glowing with ember cracks perched over hissing volcanic vents at dusk, while a small numeral 6 knight in a blue cape urges a goat-drawn stone cart piled with shimmering glass salamanders toward safety.
